text:
Harper: hey all, first-day snag. On an Android hotspot (T-Mobile) — VPN connects but trying to use internal web apps times out. I can ssh to bastion but browser to http://internal.app hangs. docker pull times out too. anyone seen hotspot/tethering weirdness?

Sam: welcome! mobile carriers often block or NAT weirdly. Two quick options: 1) make an SSH dynamic SOCKS proxy: `ssh -D 1080 bastion` and point browser to SOCKS5 127.0.0.1:1080; 2) forward corp HTTP proxy port over SSH so Docker and other tools can use it.

Harper: started `ssh -D 1080 bastion` — browser works when I set Firefox to SOCKS5 127.0.0.1:1080. docker still fails with TLS handshake timeout on pulls.

Ravi: Docker doesn't use SOCKS by default. For Docker Desktop on Mac/Windows you can set HTTP/HTTPS proxy in settings to `http://localhost:3128` if you forward a local port to the corp proxy, e.g.: `ssh -L 3128:internal.proxy.redwood:3128 bastion`. Then set Docker proxy to localhost:3128 and restart Docker.

Harper: tried `ssh -L 3128:internal.proxy.redwood:3128 bastion` and set Docker Desktop -> Settings -> Resources -> Proxies -> HTTP proxy = http://localhost:3128. After restart docker pull started immediately. Nice!

Megan: alternative for Linux laptop: use `proxytunnel` or `tsocks` wrappers, or `redsocks` + iptables to redirect outbound traffic to the SOCKS5. But the SSH forward to corp proxy is usually easiest for short-term tethered setups.

Harper: is it safe to bind 3128 to localhost like that? worried about leaving open on public wifi.

Sam: binding to localhost is fine for short sessions. If you use `-L 127.0.0.1:3128:internal.proxy.redwood:3128` you're explicit. Don't use `0.0.0.0` on untrusted networks.

Harper: oh and my SSH session sometimes gets dropped by the hotspot after ~10m and my dynamic proxy dies. any keepalive tips?

Ravi: add to `~/.ssh/config`: `Host bastion*\n  ServerAliveInterval 30\n  ServerAliveCountMax 4\n  TCPKeepAlive yes`. Also try `-o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes` when creating forwards to avoid orphaned sessions. If carrier aggressively terminates, try `autossh -M 0 -f -N -D 1080 bastion` to auto-reconnect.

Harper: perfect. one more Q: who do I ask for a permanent exception so the hotspot works without these hacks?

infra-bot: Automated: please open a ticket in #infra with your device + region + example traceroute/pcap. Created INFRA-5001 "Investigate mobile hotspot connectivity for VPN users" (https://redwood.internal/infra/5001).

Megan: for long-term we usually prefer issuing a dev-proxy route (secure proxy that accepts TLS on 443) instead of changing infra firewall rules. Ping #infra with your ticket if you want that.

Harper: thanks everyone, saved these commands to my onboarding notes. going to try autossh next. :raised_hands:
